title: Lemon Custard Ice Cream with Blackberry Ripple
changes_from_base: Lemon peel steeped in the dairy instead of vanilla; a reduced blackberry syrup rippled through after churning.
summary: Our classic custard infused with lemon peel instead of vanilla, then rippled with a reduced blackberry syrup after churning. Fresh, tart and striking to look at.

ingredients.item: lemons, zest pared in wide strips (about 8 g)
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Steep the lemon
steps.text: Heat the cream and milk with the lemon strips until steaming, then cover off the heat for 45 min. Peel holds the lemon oils, so the dairy tastes of lemon without curdling from the juice.

steps.title: Make the ripple
steps.text: Meanwhile, blend or mash the blackberries, push through the sieve and discard the seeds. Simmer the juice with 60 g sugar in the small pan, stirring, for 8-10 min until reduced to about 120 ml, then chill; reducing it stops the ripple freezing into icy streaks.

steps.title: Prepare the yolks
steps.text: Whisk the yolks with 120 g sugar. Lift out the lemon strips and rewarm the dairy until steaming.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Whisk two ladles of the lemon dairy into the yolks and return to the pan.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Keep stirring over a gentle flame until the custard thickens enough to coat the spatula, at 77-80 °C. Avoid boiling.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Season with the salt, strain into a clean bowl, set it over the iced water to cool, then chill for 4 h or more.

steps.title: Churn and ripple
steps.text: Churn until thick, then layer it into the container with spoonfuls of the cold blackberry syrup and drag a knife through once or twice. Too much swirling blends the colours into pink.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Freeze for at least 4 h until scoopable.

tips: Pare the lemon with a vegetable peeler, leaving the bitter white pith behind.
A common mistake is skipping the reduction, so the syrup freezes hard and icy. Simmer it until syrupy.
Raspberries make an equally good ripple.
storage: Freeze, covered, for up to 2 weeks.
